slides.title: Medicare has more than [[one]] enrollment window.
slides.body: Mixing them up can be expensive.

slides.title: October 15 to December 7
slides.body:
Changes take effect January 1.
This is the window for reviewing and switching coverage [[you already have]].

slides.title: The window to watch is the [[first]] one.
slides.body: About 7 months around your 65th birthday: 3 months before, your birthday month, and 3 months after.

slides.title: Late enrollment can follow you.
slides.body: Skip Part B or Part D when you're first eligible, without other qualifying coverage, and a penalty can be added to your premium. In many cases, for as long as you have that coverage.

slides.title: Current employer coverage may let you [[wait]].
slides.body:
A Special Enrollment Period can follow when the job or coverage ends.
Usually doesn't count: COBRA and retiree coverage.

slides.title: Have an HSA?
slides.body:
Contributions have to stop before Medicare begins, and Part A can start retroactively.
Talk with your CPA about the timing.

slides.title: Ask before you retire:
items: When does my Initial Enrollment Period start?
Does my HSA need a stop date?
What happens to my spouse's coverage?

slides.title:
Retirement is a date you choose.
Medicare has dates that [[choose for you]].
